Skeletal system.description: The body system of bones and cartilage that supports the body, protects organs, facilitates movement, produces blood cells, and stores minerals.

Joints.description: The body’s articulations, where bones meet; their structure determines stability and permitted movement.

Teeth.description: Mineralized oral structures used to cut, tear, and grind food during mastication.

Rotator cuff muscles.description: The four shoulder muscles whose tendons blend with the glenohumeral capsule to stabilize the humeral head while it moves.

Nucleus pulposus.description: The hydrated, gelatinous core of an intervertebral disc; it resists compression and helps distribute spinal loads.

Internal abdominal oblique muscle.description: A lateral abdominal-wall muscle whose fibers help compress abdominal contents and assist trunk movement.

Rectus anterior capitis muscle.description: A small prevertebral neck muscle that flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

Rectus lateralis capitis muscle.description: A small lateral atlanto-occipital muscle that assists lateral flexion and stabilizes the head.

Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.description: The humeral origin of flexor carpi ulnaris, a forearm muscle that flexes and adducts the wrist.

Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.description: The humeroulnar origin of flexor digitorum superficialis, which flexes the fingers at the proximal interphalangeal joints.

Interosseous membrane.description: A fibrous connective-tissue sheet between paired long bones that helps bind them and transmits load.

Parathyroid gland.description: An endocrine gland that secretes parathyroid hormone, a key regulator of blood calcium concentration.

Hypophysis.description: The pituitary gland, an endocrine organ at the brain’s base that releases hormones controlling multiple body functions.

Pubic hairs.description: Keratinized hair shafts arising from follicles in the pubic skin.

Hairs of head.description: Keratinized hair shafts arising from follicles of the scalp.

Skeleton of upper limbs.description: The bones of the upper limbs, providing the framework for shoulder, arm, forearm, wrist, and hand movement.

Bones of free part of lower limb.description: The bones distal to the pelvic girdle that form the thigh, leg, ankle, and foot.

Lymphoid organs.description: The organs and tissues that produce, house, or coordinate immune cells and lymphatic immune responses.

Left lobe of thymus.description: One lobe of the thymus, a primary lymphoid organ where T lymphocytes mature.

Right lobe of thymus.description: One lobe of the thymus, a primary lymphoid organ where T lymphocytes mature.

Tracheobronchial tree.description: The branching conducting airway system from the trachea through the bronchi within the lungs.

Superior parathyroid gland.description: One of the parathyroid glands, which secretes parathyroid hormone to help regulate blood calcium concentration.

Accessory parotid gland.description: A variable, separate focus of salivary tissue anterior to the main parotid gland; it may drain through a secondary duct.

Ciliary body-curve.description: The ciliary body is part of the vascular middle layer of the eye; it contributes to aqueous-humor production and contains the ciliary muscle.

rules.description: The hyaline cartilage at the anterior end of the named rib, providing a flexible connection within the thoracic cage.
The hydrated, gelatinous core of the intervertebral disc at this named spinal level; it resists compression and helps distribute load.
A named dense connective-tissue band that links the indicated skeletal structures and contributes to joint stability.
The fibrous capsule enclosing the named synovial joint; its inner synovial membrane surrounds the fluid-filled joint cavity.
A synovial fluid-filled sac in the named location that reduces friction between adjacent moving tissues.
A synovial or fibrous sheath associated with the named tendon, reducing friction as the tendon moves through a confined path.
A ligament located between adjacent bones that supports their articulation and limits separation.
A named ligament of the indicated joint complex that reinforces the articulation and guides or limits movement.
A regional lymph node or group of nodes that filters lymph from its drainage territory and participates in adaptive immune responses.
A named vein that carries blood from its drainage territory toward the heart; venous patterns can vary between individuals.
A leaflet of the named cardiac valve; valve leaflets open with forward pressure and close to prevent reverse blood flow.

rules.pattern: ^(Left|Right) (surface of heart|inferior border of heart|apex of heart|inferior interventricular sulcus|root of pulmonary trunk|atrioventricular valve)$
rules.description: A named external landmark or valvular structure of the heart used to identify cardiac chambers, vessels, or blood-flow boundaries.

rules.pattern: (gyrus|sulcus|fissure|occipital lobe|globus pallidus|lentiform nucleus|mamillary body|Base of peduncle|Aqueduct of midbrain|Central canal|funiculus|fasciculus)
rules.description: A named neuroanatomical landmark or neural pathway in the brain or spinal cord; its identity localizes the structure within the central nervous system.

rules.pattern: (lobule|vermis|Declive|Uvula of vermis|Pyramis of vermis|Folium of vermis|Peduncle of flocculus)$
rules.description: A named subdivision or surface landmark of the cerebellum, the brain region that integrates sensory feedback with motor activity.
A named peripheral nerve that carries neural fibers between the nervous system and its indicated anatomical territory.

rules.pattern: (region|surfaces of digits|Dorsum of |Sole$|border of |groove|foveola|fold$|arch of foot|eminence|fossa|Apex of auricle|Auricular tubercle)
rules.description: A named surface anatomical area or landmark used to describe the location of structures on the body.
The visible hard keratin plate of the nail, produced by the nail matrix and lying over the nail bed.
The soft tissue bordering the nail plate, forming part of the protective nail unit.
Keratinized hair shafts arising from follicles in the eyebrow skin.
A regional lymph node or group of nodes that filters lymph from its drainage territory and participates in adaptive immune responses.
A lateral abdominal-wall muscle whose fibers help compress abdominal contents and assist trunk movement.
A named connective-tissue partition or arch that separates or transmits structures in the indicated limb region.
A named articulation or articulation group; its connective tissues join the indicated skeletal elements and determine permitted movement.
A named muscle group or muscle subdivision in the indicated region, represented to show its anatomical location.
A synovial fold within the hip-joint capsule that carries vessels toward the femoral head.
A named component of the peripheral nervous system that carries or contains neural fibers outside the brain and spinal cord.

rules.pattern: (Central structures of spinal cord|Intermediate zone of spinal cord|Intermediomedial nucleus|Spinal reticular process)
rules.description: A named spinal-cord region or nucleus used to localize gray or white matter within the central nervous system.
A rounded inferior lobule on the cerebellar hemisphere, part of the cerebellum’s surface anatomy.
